findings.how_to_check: In 1c_tgt_divided_files.do before line 111, run: count if name_true_cleaned_exists==0 & !(f_name==f_ans & l_name==l_ans) & !tgt and tabulate tgt among the discrepant records. After running MATCHING/_tgt_only_run.do, merge link1930_1940_mltgt1940_cleaned_noraceblock0.dta and link1930_1940_ml1940_cleaned_noraceblock0.dta by ID to verify whether any linked pair, or non-unique candidate pair, involves these 436 IDs.
findings.suggested_fix: Reconcile the upstream cleaning discrepancy between divided_file1940_true_cleaned and divided_file1940_ans_cleaned so nbad==0 before producing final links. If running temporarily, verify how many of the 436 records are non-targets vs targets, and confirm that none of them alter linked pairs or candidate competition in the resulting link datasets.
findings.title: Permitted fallback discrepancies can make linkage runs differ for reasons other than model-name targeting
findings.what_the_code_does: The code accumulates fallback discrepancies where name_true_cleaned_exists==0 & !(f_name==f_ans & l_name==l_ans) into nbad, but replaces the previous fatal assertion exit with a non-fatal threshold check: if `nbad' > 0.001*`nchk' exit 459. For the observed 436 discrepancies out of 1,031,654 checked records, the script logs a NOTE and continues. For any of these 436 records that are non-targets (!tgt), lines 111-114 overwrite f_name and l_name with _ans_cleaned values, while the all-records baseline (_true_cleaned) keeps the differing fallback names. Conversely, for any of the 436 that are targets (tgt), lines 111-114 do not run, leaving them with _true_cleaned fallback names rather than _ans_cleaned names.
findings.why_it_matters: The explicit purpose of generating _tgt_cleaned alongside _true_cleaned in MATCHING/_tgt_only_run.do:8-9 is so that the two runs 'differ only in which 1940 records get model names'. When non-target records have differing Ancestry fallback names between the two runs, any observed difference in links or match rates between target-only and all-records is partly attributable to discrepancies in fallback cleaning rather than pure model targeting. In addition, because ABE linkage requires candidate uniqueness within age/birthplace cells, changes in candidate names can spill over to competing potential matches. Although 436 records is only ~0.042% of checked records, tolerating them without classifying them by tgt leaves the counterfactual contrast slightly confounded.

review_limits: No paper draft was supplied, so paper claims could not be checked against the code; claims-vs-code review was limited to statements in code comments and the supplied review brief.
Data files in external directories ($REP_F, $REP_SNU) are gitignored and not accessible, so the 436 fallback discrepancies could not be inspected directly or classified into targets vs non-targets.
The Stata runtime environment and pipeline could not be executed; runtime conclusions are based on Stata source code analysis and counts reported in the review briefs.
Review was scoped to the uncommitted working tree diff against HEAD and untracked files shown in git status --short, rather than a full-repository audit.
structured_output.summary: The relaxation of the fallback check in 1c_tgt_divided_files.do to a 0.1% tolerance threshold is syntactically sound and allows the target-only linkage run to proceed without failing on the 436 known discrepancies. However, tolerating these discrepancies means the target-only and all-record linkage runs differ not only by model-name targeting, but also by differing Ancestry fallback cleaning on non-target records (and target records without model names will differ from the Ancestry baseline). Before finalizing paper exhibits, the author should classify the 436 records by target status and verify that they do not materially alter link formation or candidate uniqueness in the linkage comparisons.

For the observed count of 436 out of 1,031,654 records (0.042%), 436 > 1031.654 evaluates to false, emitting the warning note without aborting execution.

summary.description: Two to four sentences. The overall state of the reviewed work and the single most important thing to fix. No preamble.

dimensions_reviewed.description: Which scope dimensions were actually reviewed in this run.

findings.description: Defects and concerns, ordered most severe first. Empty if none. Do not pad with stylistic observations.

severity.description: blocker: a reported result is wrong. major: a referee would demand it. minor: real but survivable. nit: cosmetic.

confidence.description: verified: traced in the source. likely: strongly implied but depends on unseen data. speculative: a question, not an established defect.

title.description: One line, stating the defect itself, not its category.

location.description: path:line, or path:line-line. Several may be comma-separated. Required: a finding without a location is not a finding.

what_the_code_does.description: Precisely what the code computes, quoting the relevant expression. Contrast with what it was evidently intended to compute.

why_it_matters.description: The consequence for a number or claim in the paper. If there is no consequence, the severity is nit.

how_to_check.description: A concrete command, tabulation, or count the author can run to confirm or refute this in minutes.

suggested_fix.description: The change, specific enough to act on. Do not apply it yourself.

verified_clean.description: Things explicitly checked that were fine. This is what makes a short findings list trustworthy rather than lazy.

evidence.description: How it was confirmed, with path:line where applicable.

review_limits.description: What this review could NOT establish: data not readable, pipeline not runnable, paper text unavailable, Stata semantics not verifiable by reading. Be explicit; silence here reads as false assurance.
